flags.name: Flag 1 - XSS
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-WAF-XSS — Cross-Site Scripting against shop.soledrop.co (WAF ML score) in the Alert name column.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="30">The flag is the number of alerts in this cluster.</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 2 - XSS
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left. 
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-WAF-XSS — Cross-Site Scripting against shop.soledrop.co (WAF ML score) in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Use the Purple AI Alert Description to find the MITRE ATT&CK reference associated with exploitation of public-facing applications.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="T####">The flag is the MITRE ATT&CK ID</s1-flag>

hints.description:
Read through the Purple AI Alert Description.

Find the MITRE ATT&CK ID that comes right before (exploitation of public-facing applications).

The code follows the following format: T####.

flags.name: Flag 3 - XSS - Workflow
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left. 
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-WAF-XSS — Cross-Site Scripting against shop.soledrop.co (WAF ML score) in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>

Click on the Automate button in the top right of the Alert popup.

HyperAutomation workflows allow Threat Hunters to enrich alerts, gather third-party threat intel, seek out determinitions from analysts, and conduct follow-up responses automatically whenever alerts are triggered.

</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="S1-CNAPP-AppAttack">The flag is the name of the workflow under 'Available Workflows'</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 4 - CF Integration
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left. 
  
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-WAF-XSS — Cross-Site Scripting against shop.soledrop.co (WAF ML score) in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts.

Find the Available HyperAutomation workflow from the Automation tab.
</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>

Open the available HA workflow. Workflows fire actions in order from top to bottom. What is the first action that calls the Cloudflare API?

</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="CF Create IP Rule">The flag is the name of the Cloudflare integration.</s1-flag>

hints.description: Starting at the top, scroll down to find the first action that displays 'Cloudflare' with their logo.
The flag is <s1-answer>CF JD Cloud IP Details</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 5 - Workflow Conditional
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left. 
  
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-WAF-XSS — Cross-Site Scripting against shop.soledrop.co (WAF ML score) in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts.

Find the Available HyperAutomation workflow from the Automation tab.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Find the action labeled CF Ruleset Host Block.

This action has already ran. Look in the Body section to see the JSON body that was returned. What action was taken?

</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="">The flag is the value of the action field.</s1-flag>

hints.description:
The action field is the very first field in the JSON body.

The value of the action field is highlighted orange.

flags.name: Flag 6 - CF Block IP
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left. 
  
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-WAF-XSS — Cross-Site Scripting against shop.soledrop.co (WAF ML score) in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts.

Find the Available HyperAutomation workflow from the Automation tab.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Under the Cloudflare Block IP action, what HTTP method and body are sent?
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="GET /api/body/etc">The flag is the HTTP method and body sent by this action.</s1-flag>

hints.description:
Find the Cloudflare integrated action named Cloudflare Block IP action.

The flag is located in the description at the top of the popup.

flags.name: Flag 7 - Credential Stuffing
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-Access-CredStuffing — Login Brute Force / Credential Stuffing on portal.soledrop.co in the Alert name column.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="30">The flag is the number of alerts in this cluster.</s1-flag>

<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left. 
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-Access-CredStuffing — Login Brute Force / Credential Stuffing on portal.soledrop.co in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Use the Purple AI Alert Description to find the MITRE ATT&CK reference associated with Password Guessing.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="T####.###">The flag is the MITRE ATT&CK ID</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 9 - VirusTotal
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left. 
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-Access-CredStuffing — Login Brute Force / Credential Stuffing on portal.soledrop.co in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Find the alert in this cluster that has been marked as True Positive under the Analyst Verdict column.

Find the Notes section of this alert.

According to VirusTotal, how many security vendors have labeled this IP as malicious?
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="10">The flag is the number of security vendors who've labeled this IP as malicious.</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 10 - URL of target Site
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left.
  
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-Access-CredStuffing — Login Brute Force / Credential Stuffing on portal.soledrop.co in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts.

Find the alert in this cluster that has been marked as True Positive under the Analyst Verdict column.

Find the Notes section of this alert.
</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>

Look for the Source IP associated with this Brute Force attack. Where did this IP send the attack to?

</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="____.soledrop.co">The flag is URL of the site being targeted.</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 11 - Rule JSON Body
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate to HyperAutomation. Open the workflow designated 'See WAF Rule'. Click on the 'Get Firewall Rules' Actoon. Click the 'Test Action' button.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Look at the Test Output.

What is the id of the firewall rule that logs all Login attempts?
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="5668406f0a644a50bc9e86a561a72650">The flag is the id value.</s1-flag>

hints.description:
Use Ctrl-F or the magnifying glass to find the section of the output pertaining logins.

The id is the very first field in that respective JSON body.

flags.name: Flag 12 - CF Firewall Rules
flags.description:
<s1-nav>In the Cloudflare console, find the Domains dropdown and select find the Overview page. From the Overview page, find the soledrop.co domain. Find the Security dropdown from the menus the left and go to Security Rules.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
On the Cloudflare side, what is the name of the security rule that logs all Login attempts?
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="WAF-Recon-Log: Log scanner">The flag is the name of the security rule.</s1-flag>

hints.description: The description of this rule says: <s1-value>URI Path contains /login and Request Method equals POST</s1-value>
The flag is <s1-answer>WAF-LoginLog: Log all login POSTs</s1-answer>.
